turns.doctor_question: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?
turns.patient_response:
Hi. Nice to meet you too. I'm here because... well, I spend most of my day just going back over the same things in the house. The outlets, the locks, my tools... even the dust. I just keep checking them and fixing them, again and again. 

I do it until I'm completely worn out, but I still just don't feel sure enough to leave it alone. It takes up my whole day. So, that's why I'm here.

symptom_reasoning.S066: The patient describes spending most of the day repetitively checking and fixing household items such as outlets, locks, and tools because they do not feel sure enough to leave them alone.

turns.doctor_question: When you feel the need to check these things again, is it because an unwanted thought or image keeps coming into your mind?
turns.patient_response:
Yeah, that's exactly it. Even when I know I did the job right, these... these ugly thoughts just keep jumping in. 

I'll get this picture in my head that a loose wire I missed is going to burn the whole house down, or... or that a nail I left somewhere is going to hurt my wife. I try to push them out of my head, I really do, but they just come right back stronger. And then I just have to go check again.

symptom_reasoning.S065: The patient describes intrusive, unwanted thoughts and images of harm or disaster (e.g., a loose wire burning the house down or a nail hurting his wife) that persist despite efforts to push them away.
symptom_reasoning.S066: The patient reports feeling driven to repeatedly check things ('And then I just have to go check again') in direct response to the intrusive thoughts.

turns.doctor_question: Do these thoughts feel like your own mind is producing them, even though you don’t want them?
turns.patient_response:
Yeah, I mean... I know it's my own brain doing it. It's not like someone else is putting them in there or anything. They're definitely my own thoughts. 

I just... I really don't want them. I don't know why my mind keeps coming up with this stuff, if that's what you're asking, but yeah, it's all coming from me.

turns.doctor_question: Besides checking, do you also feel driven to arrange things until they feel exactly right?
turns.patient_response: No, not really. I mean... I don't care about lining things up or making them look perfect, if that's what you mean. It's just the checking. I just need to know my tools are put away safe and the outlets aren't going to spark. I don't have to arrange them in any special order or anything like that. So, no, I don't really do that.

symptom_reasoning.S066: The patient confirms engaging in checking compulsions (verifying tools are safe and outlets won't spark), while clarifying they do not perform ordering or arranging rituals.

I do it until I'm completely worn out, and... and even then, I still don't feel sure enough to just leave it alone. So, yeah, I know it's excessive. That's honestly why I'm here.

turns.doctor_question: Outside of the checking, do you spend a lot of time worrying about many different everyday things?
turns.patient_response:
Not really, no. I mean... I guess I just don't have the time or energy for normal worries. My head is pretty much completely focused on the checking stuff. 

I don't sit around stressing about, you know, everyday things or what's going to happen tomorrow... unless it has to do with the house catching fire or my tools being out. That pretty much takes up everything I have. So, outside of that, no, I don't really worry about a bunch of other random stuff.

turns.doctor_question: When you go back to check things, does checking make those unwanted thoughts ease up, even for a short time?
turns.patient_response:
Maybe for a split second, but... like I said a minute ago, that's exactly why I'm here. I spend most of my day going back over the same outlets, the locks, my tools, the dust in the house... checking and fixing them again and again. 

If it gave me real relief, I wouldn't have to keep doing it until I'm completely worn out. Because even after all that checking, I still don't feel sure enough to just leave it alone. So... no, the thoughts don't really ease up in any way that lasts.
